Parliament Passes Tribunal Reforms Bill Amidst Opposition Protests

The Lok Sabha passed the Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026, which aims to improve efficiency and transparency in tribunal appointments. The bill was passed without debate amidst protests from the Opposition. One outlet reported that the government should not have the power to remove tribunal members at will. The bill places the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal (NCLAT) under a new appointment regime, while excluding the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) from its ambit. The legislation also seeks to make tribunal appointments transparent and independent.
